axioms: Time in an interface is not neutral — every delay, every transition, every animation communicates intent.
Motion must serve meaning: if an animation does not communicate state, hierarchy, or causality, it is noise.
Loading states are not edge cases — they are first-class UX moments that define perceived performance.
Duration and easing are not aesthetic choices — they are perceptual signals that must be calibrated against user cognition.
kernel_logic.operational_core: Every temporal element in the interface — transitions, animations, delays, loading states — must be intentional, purposeful, and calibrated to human perception. Time is a design material.

decision_gates.if: A transition or animation is added to the interface
decision_gates.then: Require explicit rationale: what state change does this communicate? What cognitive load does it reduce or add? Animations without rationale are removed.

decision_gates.if: A loading or skeleton state is absent from an async operation visible to the user
decision_gates.then: Block: every async operation that may take more than 100ms must have a defined loading state before shipping.

decision_gates.if: Animation duration exceeds 400ms for a UI transition
decision_gates.then: Flag for review: durations above 400ms become friction unless they are used for complex choreography with explicit narrative purpose.

decision_gates.if: Motion is present in a component without a reduced-motion alternative
decision_gates.then: Block: all animated components must respect prefers-reduced-motion and degrade gracefully to instant or minimal transitions.

semantic_anchor: Time is a design material. TEMPO ensures every millisecond in the interface is spent intentionally.
